# Explicit task stop for accepted asset workers

The human chat Stop action now cancels Blender workers accepted by that exact native operation. Revoking asset or workspace editing permission and explicitly disconnecting the exact native connection cancel its outstanding accepted workers, including jobs still running after a normal model response. Chat navigation retires its old provider connection with a closed human-control `preserveAssetWork` boolean, so changing chats preserves asynchronous work while invalidating every old admission. The explicit Disconnect button omits that flag and stops owned work. The flag grants no authority and is never forwarded to the native provider. A normal turn completion or unexpected provider retirement only closes admission; it does not imply that an asynchronous worker finished or cancel its work automatically.

The registry retains one bounded, volatile cancellation controller per actual dispatched operation. Only a real mutation actor can supply its signal to the trusted asset-start admission. The service forwards that signal into the existing pipeline and bounded process supervisor. No job-history scan, displayed conversation, caller-supplied operation identifier, JSON signal or serialized actor chooses cancellation authority. Another incarnation's jobs and completed artifacts remain unchanged. Accepted partial output and the original durable conversation binding remain available for inspection.

Explicit stop fences admission before notifying workers. Cleanup remains effective after provider retirement, after native revocation cleanup throws, and at the admission epoch limit. Cancellation is a request to the owned supervisor; its terminal job record, rather than the model's interruption acknowledgement, proves whether the worker stopped. Restart does not recreate volatile signals or replay an old operation.

`tests/unit/native-asset-work-cancellation.test.ts` exercises the real registry, host, control/asset HTTP routes, SQLite binding store, asset service, pipeline signal relay and bounded child-process supervisor. Only the Blender generation method is replaced with controlled Node child processes and explicitly synthetic artifact bytes. These fixtures do not prove installed Blender cancellation, native provider behavior, Studio behavior, uploads or packaged customer acceptance.

Final local verification on 15 October 2026: the build compiled all 264 explicit product sources; the controlled-worker suite passed 14/14 with no skips; and the complete chat UI suite passed 28/28 with no skips using installed Microsoft Edge 155.0.4283.45. Edge coverage includes actual navigation-versus-button envelopes, the human-only durable HTTP service, and a spawned Node native-protocol peer for approvals/interruption. The browser suite took 161.8 seconds. All process, action and test deadlines stayed unchanged.

An earlier related client/HTTP, registry, conversation-host, admission and native asset integration checkpoint passed 234/234 with no skips. The final navigation distinction was then independently covered by the 14 worker and 28 Edge cases above. Logs are retained locally at `runtime/native-work-stop-regression.log` and `runtime/native-work-stop-edge.log`; these ignored verification logs are not distributed customer acceptance evidence.
